title: Capillary Force Lithography for Cardiac Tissue Engineering
protocol: Clean silicon wafer with 100% ethanol or xylene.
Dry silicon wafer under O2/N2 gas.
Place silicon wafer in spin-coater at rotation speeds of 2,000-4,000 rpm.
Produce a photoresist film with a thickness of 0.3-0.5 µm.
Pattern the photoresist film using a photolithography system.
Immerse patterned photoresist-coated silicon wafers in a photoresist developing solution.
Rinse developed photoresist-coated silicon wafers with deionized water.
Deep reactive ion etch exposed silicon to form sub-micron scale ridges.
Remove remaining photoresist by placing the silicon wafer in a plasma asher system.
Cut silicon wafers with a diamond-tipped cutter into appropriately sized masters.
Clean silicon master surface with 100% ethanol or xylene.
Dry silicon master under O2/N2 gas.
Place silicon master pattern side up in a Petri dish.
Pipette 40 µl of PUA to the patterned surface for nanofabrication.
Place a sheet of 4 cm x 4 cm transparent polyester (PET) film over the dispensed PUA.
Press down on the PET sheet and spread the PUA underneath the sheet across the pattern face using a roller or flat edged surface so that the entire pattern is covered by the PUA prepolymer.
Place silicon master, prepolymer, and PET approximately 10 cm below a 20 Watt (115 V) UV light for 50 sec.
Remove PET film slowly with forceps after curing.
Cure PUA/PET nanopatterns under UV for at least 12 hr prior to use.
Place another film of PET on top of the silicon master without adding PUA and expose to UV light (λ = 365 nm) for 50 sec.
Remove PET film from the silicon master after exposure.
Rinse silicon master with 100% ethanol or xylene and dry under O2/N2 gas.
Prepare 25 mm diameter circular glass slides by placing in an ozone treatment chamber for 10 min.
Place ozone-treated glass slides onto small PDMS block for easy handling.
Apply thin layer of surface adhesion promoter with paintbrush to glass slides.
Air dry glass slides for 30 min.
Place the glass slide on a piece of printer paper.
Dispense 10 μl of polyurethane (PU) pre-polymer onto the center of a glass slide.
Ensure no bubbles are present in the dispensed PU.
Place PUA mold pattern face down on the glass slide with the PU.
Disperse the PU uniformly across the surface by rolling a rubber cylinder roller along the PUA mold.
Expose to UV lamp for polymerization.
Peel the PUA mold from the PU-coated glass slide once polymerization is complete.
Store finished samples in desiccator for up to one month.
Mix silicone elastomer base and curing agent in a 10:1 ratio vigorously.
Pour mixed PDMS precursor solution into a Petri dish, ensuring it reaches 5 mm up the edge of the dish.
Place Petri dish with PDMS precursor in a desiccator for degassing for at least one hour.
Cure the PDMS by placing the Petri dish in a 65°C oven for at least two hours.
Cut cured flat PDMS into 3 cm x 3 cm square sections using a razor.
Clean 25 mm diameter circular glass slides by placing in isopropyl alcohol for 30 min in a water sonicator.
Dry cleaned glass slides under O2/N2 gas.
Drop dispense 100 μl of PLGA solution (15% w/v PLGA in chloroform) onto glass slide.
Place a flat PDMS mold on top of the dispensed PLGA to absorb the solvent and obtain a flat PLGA surface.
Apply a light pressure (~10 kPa) by placing a 200 g weight on top of the PDMS for 5 min.
Slowly peel away flat PDMS mold and place the cover glass on a preheated plate (120 °C) for 5 min to remove residual solvent and increase adhesion between the PLGA and the cover glass.
Place the NP PUA mold on top of the flat PLGA and apply constant pressure (~100 kPa) and heat (120 °C) by placing a 1 kg weight on top of the PUA mold while on the heating plate for 15 min.
Remove the weight from PLGA cover slide and allow the substrata to cool to room temperature.
Carefully peel away the NP PUA mold once the substrata have cooled sufficiently, revealing the NP PLGA substratum.
Place finished samples in desiccator for storage for as long as a month.
Attach the ANFS coverslips (PU or PLGA) to a 35 mm tissue culture polystyrene dish.
Pipette 20 µl of Norland Optical Adhesive (NOA83H) to the bottom of the dish.
Gently place the ANFS coverslip on top of the NOA.
Allow glue to spread out and cover entire coverslip bottom.
Cure NOA by exposing dish to UV for 10 min.
Sterilize ANFS by rinsing with 2 ml of 70% aqueous ethanol solution for 5 min, twice.
Remove ethanol by aspiration.
Allow ANFS to completely air dry for ~1 hr under the UV sterilization lamp (λ = 200-290 nm) in the biological safety cabinet.
Dilute fibronectin in DI water to 5 µg/ml.
Pipette 2 ml of fibronectin solution into dish.
Place dish in incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 overnight (at least 6 hr).
Centrifuge cell sample at 1,000 rpm for 3 min to pellet the cells.
Carefully remove the supernatant by aspiration.
Resuspend cells in appropriate culture media to a concentration of 4.6 x 10^6 cells/ml.
Pipette 200 µl of cell suspension onto sterilized ANFS.
Place cells in incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 4 hr to allow cells to attach to ANFS.
Add 2 ml of warm culture media to dish.
Replace cells in incubator under the same conditions.
After 24 hr, remove media and wash with 2 ml of DPBS twice to remove excess cells.
Add 2 ml of warm culture media to dish.
Replace cells in incubator under the same conditions.
Culture the cells to confluence.
Replace media every other day.
